# Backoffice static agent-context graph

- **Static mount:** `/static/`
- **Files:** 58
- **Entry points:** 1 `SYSTEM.md` + 17 skills

## What is this

> **Agent instruction:** Always load and use the `writing-for-agents` skill when reading this
> context graph.

This graph shows how Backoffice progressively discloses guidance to its agent. Like the skill system
used by coding agents, it separates what the agent needs on every task from what it loads only when
a task calls for it.

`SYSTEM.md` provides the baseline guidance. Skill descriptions act as context pointers: they tell
the agent when to read a skill without loading its full instructions upfront. A loaded skill can
then point to references, tool declarations, or other skills for the branch of work at hand. The
trees below make those layers visible, from the entry point to deeper guidance.

Use this map when shaping the agent's instructions: what belongs in always-loaded context, what
belongs behind a skill trigger, and what should be disclosed only for a particular branch? The
wording of each pointer determines whether the agent reaches the right guidance at the right time.
The goal is to keep the initial context focused while making task-specific detail discoverable when
it is needed.

The graph is generated from `apps/backoffice/content/static/`. It shows the available paths through
checked-in guidance, not the reads an agent actually made or dynamic runtime content. Regenerate it
from the repository root with `pnpm backoffice:context`; do not edit this file manually.

## How context is loaded

- `SYSTEM.md` is injected automatically.
- Each `SKILL.md` is a top-level candidate; its description tells the agent when to load it.
- Nested paths are follow-up reads mentioned by an already loaded file.
- `__BACKOFFICE_CODEMODE_DTS__` is expanded from `/static/codemode/system.d.ts`; it is not left
  opaque.
